chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥamdān ibn Sulaymān, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Muḥammad al-Yamānī, from Manīʿ ibn al-Ḥajjāj, from Yūnus, from Hishām ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, regarding the saying:
of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Its faith shall not benefit a soul if it had not believed before.”
Meaning: during the Covenant, or it earned some good in its faith.
He said: “The acknowledgement of the Prophets, the Awṣiyāʾ, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in particular.”
He said: “Its faith will not benefit it because it was stripped away.”

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, singled out specifically in this report
key_terms.إِيمَانُهَا: its faith, whose benefit is being discussed
key_terms.الْأَنْبِيَاءِ: the Prophets whose recognition is required
key_terms.الْأَوْصِيَاءِ: the successors designated after the Prophets
key_terms.الْإِقْرَارُ: affirmation or acknowledgement as an element of faith
key_terms.الْمِيثَاقِ: the primordial Covenant in which prior affirmation is meant
key_terms.سُلِبَتْ: was stripped away or taken away

ai.seo_question: What does the verse “its faith shall not profit a soul which did not believe before” mean in relation to the Covenant and wilayah?
ai.summary: This report explains the verse as referring to a faith that does not benefit when it was not affirmed earlier, specifically in connection with the primordial Covenant. It identifies beneficial faith as including acknowledgement of the Prophets, the Awṣiyāʾ, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in particular, and states that such faith may become unavailing when it has been taken away.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hamdan Bin Suleyman, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Yamani, from Mani’e Bin Al Hajjaj, from Yunus, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[6:158] its faith shall not profit a soul, which did not believe before
– Meaning during the Covenant, or earn good through its faith.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The acknowledgement with the Prophets<sup>as</sup> and the succesors<sup>as</sup> and Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> in particular’.
Heasws said: ‘Its Eman would not benefit it because it would have been Confiscated’.
en.sarwar: 81. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from ‘Ammar al-Sabati who has said the following.

“I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most gracious. “Are those who seek God’s pleasure equal to those who incur His wrath and whose dwelling will be hell, the terrible destination? [3:162] People are of various grades in the sight of God. .” [3:163]

The Imam (a.s.) said, “Those who follow what Allah is pleased are the Imams. They, by Allah, O ‘Ammar, give grades and degrees to the true believers. By means of our Wilaya (Leadership and guardian ship with Divine Authority) and their acknowledgment of us Allah increases the reward for their good deeds and (Allah) raises them to higher positions.”
